chapter_note: Nearly the entire chapter is systematic cosmological exposition: a fourfold apportioning of the "ruling-power" across cosmic structures, followed by a mechanical rationale for suspending the leaders on the stellar wheel and an extended king/kingdom analogy to express proportional balance. Only the opening dialogue attribution is hagiographic frame; there is no NT citation or institutional/pastoral extension here (despite the chapter-level fatigue warning).

paragraphs.core_text: The wheel of the stars, which is displayed to you, is a great mighty thing! Also, it is one among the four great things; since the whole ruling-power is assigned to four parts.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks:" (hagiographic compilation formula).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a standard Kephalaia frame attribution (later editorial container), but the content after the colon is a compact structural thesis (fourfold apportioning of the ruling-power) consistent with the impersonal cosmological teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The first part is the powers who occur in the ten firmaments that exist above the wheel, and the ruling-power that is bound in them, as it is imprisoned within them in the heavens that are above.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, enumerative cosmography ("first part"), mapping cosmic regions (ten firmaments) to bound powers—systematic, non-citational exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The second part is the eight earths that are below; the four that are composite, and the four places of darkness. The second part extends from this earth, upon which mankind walks, towards the underside.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the fourfold partition with fixed cosmological geography (eight earths; four composite + four Darkness-places) and spatial extension—still internal to the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The third part is the walls and the vessels that surround the worlds. They are the four mountains and the three vessels; with what is in them, and the ruling-power that is trapped within them, and the powers who are masters over them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Characteristic substrate-style cataloguing (four mountains/three vessels) plus containment mechanics (trapped ruling-power; masters over them).

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth part is the sphere of the stars that is appointed with great diligence, as it is ordered in a [ ... m]any [ ... ]; that of the Father of Life, [and that of the Mother of] the living.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic administrative ordering attributed to primary divine hypostases (Father of Life/Mother of the living) without Gospel citation or ecclesial application; lacunae preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: Its [ ... ] very [ ... ] with diligence, because of the great and cruel powers, and the titanic figures, [who are] in it; they being suspended from it. So, all the first-born and the leaders of all the rulers, they who were existing in the three parts, these were garnered. They were collected together, seized, bound and assigned on this wheel. Each was apportioned by these three parts. They were distributed, entwined, and weighted against their companions of the same size.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-mechanics for cosmic restraint (garnered/collected/bound/assigned/weighted) in an impersonal explanatory voice; no institutional referents. Page marker removed per extraction rules.

paragraphs.core_text: Still, for its part, the wheel is equal to them in its strength; the powers of the enmity who are bound on it. Indeed, they were suspended on the circling wheel because of their cruelty; so that, due to the wind and the motion in which they go round, they comprehend not the place wherein they are set. For if they had been bound in the heavens, the heavens would not have had the strength to support them. Again, if they had been assigned on the earths, on the fixtures that are below, they also would not have had the strength to support them. Rather, they were suspended from the wheel of the circling stars; so that the power and the light that should come up from below can be received, and given to the heavenly ones above them. Conversely, whatever will fall from above, whether cold or hot, the wheel of the sphere will also take it and cast it out upon the entire earth, upon all the wood.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic cosmological engineering rationale (why the wheel, not heavens/earths; balancing forces; transfer of powers/light; distribution of cold/hot). Entirely cosmos→cosmos causal description.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, the ordinance of the wheel is in this form. For the powers who are entwined on the wheel are like this: a king mastering his kingdom by this mighty legionary force of all the leaders of the kingdom; and with all the armour of the soldiery that is collected together for him; and also with the mass of the property of the kingdom; and the beautiful lustful aspect of the women who are collected together for him; together with [ ... ] property [ ... ] and those cattle [ ... ] that have been distributed about among his retinue. Yet, if you ask about that king, he is matched with all his retinue. His retinue, for its part, is matched against his entire kingdom. Judgement shall come forth from him, vindication and condemnation, to his entire kingdom; by his wisdom, skill and strength.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Didactic analogy (king/retinue/kingdom) used to express proportional equivalence and governance; although it draws on human imagery, it functions as internal explanatory correspondence rather than pointing to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as for this king, who is matched against the measure of his entire kingdom by his wisdom, skill and strength; so also is it for the powers who are bound on the sphere as compared to the ruling-power, and the powers who exist in the entire zone. Like the king towards his retinue; so too is it that this totality is gathered to the sphere, to seven leaders, to twelve signs of the zodiac. As all the cities are gathered to the king, again they gather to the leaders of the universe. All that is done in the universe above and below: the battles and the disorders and the captivity and the hunger and the lust and the property; so shall they increase and diminish through these leaders. They are the motivaters of the whole created order; the totality being gathered in to them the way that I have told you. I have opened your eyes!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns from analogy to explicit cosmic structure (seven leaders; twelve zodiacal signs) and causation within the created order. The closing direct-address flourish is rhetorically late-sounding, but it does not pivot to church discipline or Gospel citation, so the paragraph still reads as continuous cosmological instruction.
